jobs.title: Environmental Scientist (NEC)
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Environmental Scientist will undertake specialised environmental science duties involving the investigation, assessment and monitoring of environmental conditions, including soil, water, land and other natural resources.

The position will contribute to the identification of environmental risks, assessment of potential environmental impacts and development of appropriate management and mitigation strategies.

The successful candidate will work both independently and collaboratively with operational personnel, management, contractors and relevant stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

The successful applicant will be responsible for:

* Conducting environmental field investigations, inspections and scientific assessments to identify existing environmental conditions and potential environmental risks.
* Collecting, analysing and interpreting soil, water and other environmental samples to assess contamination, pollution levels and environmental quality.
* Monitoring environmental conditions and evaluating the impacts of operational and project activities on surrounding land, water, ecosystems and natural resources.
* Undertaking environmental assessments and investigations to identify potential impacts associated with construction, civil works, land disturbance and other operational activities.
* Developing, implementing and reviewing environmental management plans, procedures and control measures to minimise adverse environmental impacts.
* Identifying environmental hazards, non-compliance issues and potential risks, and recommending appropriate corrective and preventative actions.
* Providing scientific advice and technical recommendations to management regarding environmental protection, pollution prevention, land management and environmental compliance.
* Preparing detailed environmental assessment reports, technical documentation, monitoring reports and recommendations based on scientific findings and collected data.
* Assessing environmental data, identifying trends and interpreting scientific results to support operational and environmental management decisions.
* Monitoring the effectiveness of environmental control measures and recommending improvements where necessary.
* Assisting with the development and implementation of environmental rehabilitation, remediation and land restoration strategies where required.
* Ensuring environmental activities are conducted in accordance with applicable Western Australian and Commonwealth environmental legislation, regulations, standards and guidelines.
* Liaising with regulatory authorities, environmental consultants, laboratories, contractors and other relevant stakeholders regarding environmental matters.
* Maintaining accurate records of environmental inspections, sampling activities, monitoring results, investigations and corrective actions.
* Providing environmental guidance and technical support to operational personnel to promote environmental awareness and responsible workplace practices.
* Investigating environmental incidents, assessing their potential impacts and recommending appropriate remedial and preventative measures.
* Essential Qualifications

Applicants must possess:

* A Bachelor Degree or higher qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Soil Science or another highly relevant environmental science discipline.
* Demonstrated technical knowledge of environmental assessment, scientific investigation and environmental monitoring.
* Strong understanding of soil and water sampling, environmental testing and scientific data analysis.
* Knowledge of relevant environmental legislation, regulatory requirements and environmental management principles.

Essential Skills and Experience

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* Relevant professional experience in environmental science, environmental investigations or a closely related scientific discipline.
* Experience undertaking environmental fieldwork, inspections and sampling activities.
* Ability to analyse and interpret scientific and environmental data.
* Experience preparing technical reports and environmental documentation.
* Knowledge of environmental risk identification, impact assessment and mitigation strategies.
* Understanding of environmental compliance requirements and environmental management systems.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving and technical report-writing skills.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple responsibilities.
* Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
* A practical approach to identifying environmental issues and developing scientifically supported solutions.

Pay: $79,423.00 – $90,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Visa sponsorship

Experience:

* Environmental services: 3 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Land
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

**Come grow with us.**

AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.

Our highly regarded Environmental team in Melbourne is seeking Professional Environmental Scientist/ Engineer with experience with Contaminated land investigations and remediation to support a range of exciting and meaningful projects across the energy, resources, Infrastructure and defence sectors.

**What will a day in this role look like:**

* Delivering fieldwork across ground remediation and contaminated land projects, including site investigations, remediation works, validation sampling and monitoring across the Victoria
* Managing field projects, including supervising contractors and mentoring graduates onsite
* Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-quality, client-focused outcomes
* Engaging with clients, regulators, and stakeholders to support project delivery
* Contributing to a positive team culture and collaborative, knowledge-sharing environment

  
**Qualifications**

The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes, you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

**What are we looking for from you?**

* A degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field, and a valid Australian driver’s licence
* Willingness to undertake regular fieldwork across contaminated land and remediation projects, including site investigations, remediation works and monitoring programs
* Around 2- 5 years experience in ground remediation, including contaminated land assessment, soil and groundwater remediation or related field-based work ideally
* Able to work independently, manage competing priorities and get involved across a wide range of projects while contributing to a supportive, team-focused environment
* Excellent communication skills – both written and verbal – with the ability to translate technical concepts clearly
* A collaborative mindset and the ability to work independently when needed
* A proactive attitude, curiosity to learn, and a commitment to delivering quality work

  
**Additional Information**

**Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?**

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Learn more about life at AECOM: LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram, X, YouTube - explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. ***To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.***

AECOM acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which we, our clients and our communities live and work around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. We are committed to connecting to Country in our work through meaningful engagement with First Nations peoples and businesses. Find out more about our Australian Reconciliation Action Plan here: https://aecom.com/au/our-vision-for-reconciliation/.
